package_info.why_malicious: The Carbanak malware, as adapted and deployed by FIN7, is engineered to gain unauthorized administrative access to victim systems, exfiltrate payment card data, and facilitate large-scale financial theft. Its deployment is exclusively for malicious purposes, including credential theft, lateral movement, memory scraping of POS systems, and covert data exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

execution_context.file_location: malicious file attached to phishing email (e.g., .doc, .exe, .lnk)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious macro or executable payload (e.g., embedded in Office document or disguised executable) that, when opened, downloads and executes the Carbanak malware. The macro may use VBA to invoke PowerShell or cmd.exe to retrieve a remote payload, or the executable may directly connect to a remote server to download the main Carbanak binary.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the malicious attachment, the code executes a macro or drops an executable, which initiates a network connection to a remote server, downloads the Carbanak malware payload, writes it to disk, and executes it, resulting in initial infection and persistence setup.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros or executables in email attachments that initiate outbound network connections and download additional payloads are a well-established vector for malware delivery and are rarely present in legitimate business workflows.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate business documents should not contain macros or executables that download and execute additional software, especially from external sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in tightly controlled internal environments may use macros, but these are strictly limited and never download or execute remote code.
key_indicators: Presence of macros or embedded executables in email attachments
Execution of PowerShell or cmd.exe from within a document
Immediate outbound network connections to untrusted domains/IPs after document open
Dropping and executing files in user-accessible directories (e.g., %TEMP%, C:\Users\Public\)
Creation of persistence mechanisms (e.g., registry run keys, scheduled tasks) immediately after execution

execution_context.file_location: installed malware binary on victim endpoint (e.g., C:\Users\Public\carbanak.exe)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Carbanak core module: establishes encrypted command-and-control (C2) channel, injects into system and POS processes, enumerates running processes to identify POS software, scrapes memory for payment card data (Track 1/2), and exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled servers using HTTP(S) or custom protocols.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial execution, the malware establishes an encrypted C2 connection to attacker infrastructure, injects itself into running POS and system processes, scans the memory of POS applications for payment card data patterns, collects the data, and exfiltrates it to remote servers controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Memory scraping of POS software and exfiltration of raw payment card data are hallmark behaviors of POS malware and are never performed by legitimate business applications.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or extract raw cardholder data from process memory, nor should it establish covert C2 channels or exfiltrate sensitive data to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or forensic tools may access process memory for analysis, but such tools are not present on POS endpoints in production and never exfiltrate data.
key_indicators: Process injection into POS or financial software processes
Memory scraping for card data patterns (Track 1/2 magnetic stripe data)
Creation of outbound encrypted connections to non-corporate or suspicious domains/IPs
Exfiltration of large volumes of data to external servers
Persistence mechanisms to maintain access after reboot (e.g., service installation, registry modifications)

attack_chain.action: Phishing email with a malicious attachment (Office document with macro or disguised executable) is sent to the target; the user is socially engineered to open the file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial infection and execution of the dropper payload

attack_chain.action: The malicious macro or executable initiates a network connection to a remote server, downloads the Carbanak malware payload, writes it to disk, and executes it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of persistence and command-and-control (C2) channel

attack_chain.action: The Carbanak malware establishes an encrypted C2 connection, injects into POS and system processes, and scrapes memory for payment card data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection and preparation of payment card data for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrated payment card data is sent to attacker-controlled servers using encrypted channels for monetization.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sale of stolen card data on underground markets

behavioral_signatures: Execution of macros or unknown executables from email attachments that initiate outbound network connections
Invocation of PowerShell or cmd.exe from within Office documents
Creation of persistence mechanisms (e.g., registry run keys, scheduled tasks) immediately after document open
Process injection into POS or financial software processes
Memory scraping for Track 1/2 payment card data patterns in POS process memory
Outbound encrypted connections to known or suspicious C2 infrastructure
Exfiltration of large volumes of data to external servers, especially from POS endpoints
file_indicators: Office documents with embedded macros received via email
Unknown executables dropped in user or public directories (e.g., %TEMP%, C:\Users\Public\carbanak.exe)
Malware binaries named to mimic legitimate software (e.g., carbanak.exe, pos.exe)
Creation of new scheduled tasks or registry run keys shortly after document open
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains/IPs associated with Carbanak/FIN7 C2 infrastructure
Unusual HTTPS or HTTP POST requests to non-corporate servers immediately after document open
Encrypted data transfers from POS endpoints to external IPs/domains
Beaconing behavior to remote servers at regular intervals
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of macros or unknown executables from email attachments, especially those that invoke PowerShell or cmd.exe and initiate outbound network connections. Detect creation of persistence mechanisms (e.g., registry run keys, scheduled tasks) immediately after document open. Monitor for process injection and memory scraping behaviors targeting POS software, and alert on detection of Track 1/2 card data patterns in process memory. Use threat intelligence to block or alert on connections to known Carbanak/FIN7 C2 domains/IPs. Monitor for large or unusual outbound data transfers from POS systems, and correlate with process activity to identify exfiltration attempts.
